rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description opens with a sentence stating an action performed by a role, and its last sentence gives alternative outcomes of a verdict that decides how the process ends: Model an explicit start event before the first stated action. Model each stated action as its own task, in order. Give each alternative outcome its own branch after the decision gateway, and end each branch with an end event, so the process has a defined beginning and a defined end for every outcome.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description opens with a sentence stating an action performed by a role, and its last sentence gives alternative outcomes of a verdict that decides how the process ends

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description is written in one natural language, and the generated activity labels would be written in a different language or translated into another wording.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a sequence in which one participant hands an item to another participant, the other participant then reviews it, and the description ends with an either-or choice between two outcomes: Model one start event at the beginning of the sequence, not a separate start or end event for each step. Chain the actions as tasks in the order stated, including the handoff task of the first participant, then the review task. After the review, place one exclusive gateway whose outgoing branches lead to the two outcome tasks. Each outcome either ends its own branch or converges on a shared end. Do not add a start event for the receiving side and do not end the process after an intermediate handoff.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a sequence in which one participant hands an item to another participant, the other participant then reviews it, and the description ends with an either-or choice between two outcomes

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one participant sends a decision or document to another participant, and the other participant then reviews or acts on it as a later step: Model the sending step as its own task performed by the sending participant, placed before the receiving participant's review task, so that every stated action appears as a task in the described order. Do not omit a hand-off sentence because it seems to be only a transfer of information. If the two participants are in different pools, connect the send task to the receiving side with a message flow, not a sequence flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one participant sends a decision or document to another participant, and the other participant then reviews or acts on it as a later step

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents two or more mutually exclusive alternative activities, each of which by itself leads to the same next step or end event, so that either alternative is sufficient: Model an exclusive (XOR) gateway that routes the flow into one of the alternative activities, if the preceding point chooses between them. Connect each alternative activity to a single exclusive merge gateway, and connect that merge gateway to the shared next step or end event. Do not connect alternatives directly to the shared step or end event, and do not use a parallel gateway for alternatives that exclude each other.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents two or more mutually exclusive alternative activities, each of which by itself leads to the same next step or end event, so that either alternative is sufficient
rules_sent_back.source: learned guideline (refines GW-03), generalized from EXS-006

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one participant sends a decision or document to another participant, and a later activity of the receiving participant acts on it: Model the sending as an explicit task in the sender's pool or lane, placed before the receiver's activity. If the receiver belongs to a different participant, connect the sending task to the receiving side with a message flow. Do not omit the sending step or reduce it to an implicit message flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one participant sends a decision or document to another participant, and a later activity of the receiving participant acts on it
